best_for: Minecraft Java players who juggle modpacks or several game versions and want each setup kept in its own clean instance, on Windows, Mac or Linux.
description:
Prism Launcher is a Minecraft launcher built by a community of contributors. It is made with the Qt toolkit, not an embedded web browser, so it uses very few system resources.

You can sign in with more than one Minecraft account. Modpacks can come from ATLauncher, FTB, Modrinth or Technic, browsed from the launcher's Add Instance menu, or imported from a .zip or .mrpack file you already downloaded. If you have packs in the FTB App, Prism can import them too. The menu can be rearranged and the look changed with custom themes. Coming from MultiMC, the wiki walks you through moving over.

points.title: One instance per setup
points.text: Each instance has its own Minecraft version, mods and settings, so a heavily modded pack and a vanilla world never get in each other's way.

points.title: Mods from Modrinth and CurseForge
points.text: Prism installs and updates modpacks for you, and lets you add or update single mods straight from Modrinth and CurseForge.

points.title: Java handled for you
points.text: Since version 9.0 the launcher can detect the right Java version and download Mojang's Java automatically, on Windows, macOS and Linux. Some packages leave that option out.

points.title: Free and community run
points.text: Prism is GPL-3.0 open source, funded through Open Collective and sponsors, and not affiliated with Mojang or Microsoft. It began as a fork of PolyMC, itself a fork of MultiMC.

points.title: macOS 12 or later
points.text: The Mac build is one universal zip and supports macOS Monterey or later. Older Macs can use an older Prism, but those versions are unsupported.

points.title: Windows options
points.text: Installers come for x86 and Arm64 and install per user, so no administrator rights are needed. Portable zips and MinGW builds that skip the Visual C++ runtime are also offered.

points.title: Flatpak and version history
points.text: The Linux Flatpak is verified on Flathub as the project's own, for x64 and Arm64. The Windows listing keeps 26 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.
